cues.subtitle: A Depository contract is deployed on a local test chain (an EVM). It will hold each bank's reserves and the collateral of every bilateral account, and it enforces disputes.
cues.title: The Depository is deployed
cues.tradfiParallel: The settlement system the banks hold accounts in, run as a contract instead of an operator ledger.
cues.what: A Depository contract is deployed on a local test chain (an EVM). It will hold each bank's reserves and the collateral of every bilateral account, and it enforces disputes.
cues.why: The Depository is the only shared ledger here. Payments happen in bilateral accounts; the chain is used for funding, collateral and enforcement.

cues.subtitle: Alice, Hub and Bob register on the Depository. Each bank is controlled by its own signing key.
cues.title: Three banks register
cues.tradfiParallel: Opening accounts in the settlement system before doing business.
cues.what: Alice, Hub and Bob register on the Depository. Each bank is controlled by its own signing key.
cues.why: Registration gives each bank an identity whose signatures the contract can verify.

cues.subtitle: Hub's reserve on the Depository is credited with 10,000,000 USDC of a USDC test token.
cues.title: Test balances credited on the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: Hub's reserve on the Depository is credited with 10,000,000 USDC of a USDC test token.
cues.why: A reserve is a balance held on the Depository itself. It funds collateral and on-chain transfers.

cues.subtitle: Hub queues an on-chain transfer of 3,000,000 USDC to Alice's reserve. It waits in Hub's outgoing batch.
cues.title: Hub sends Alice her test balance
cues.tradfiParallel: A transfer instruction queued before submission.
cues.what: Hub queues an on-chain transfer of 3,000,000 USDC to Alice's reserve. It waits in Hub's outgoing batch.
cues.why: In this demo the test balances come from Hub. In a deployment each bank deposits its own funds; no hub injects capital.

cues.subtitle: Hub adds 2,000,000 USDC for Bob and submits both transfers to the chain in one transaction.
cues.title: Hub sends Bob his test balance
cues.tradfiParallel: Two gross transfers in one submission.
cues.what: Hub adds 2,000,000 USDC for Bob and submits both transfers to the chain in one transaction.
cues.why: Each transfer in the batch is applied in full and on its own; the batch only shares the transaction.

cues.subtitle: The block is final: Alice holds 3,000,000 USDC and Bob 2,000,000 USDC of reserves. Hub keeps 5,000,000 USDC.
cues.title: Transfers executed on-chain
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: The block is final: Alice holds 3,000,000 USDC and Bob 2,000,000 USDC of reserves. Hub keeps 5,000,000 USDC.
cues.why: These reserves now belong to Alice and Bob, not to Hub.

cues.subtitle: Alice transfers 500,000 USDC from her reserve to Bob's on the Depository.
cues.title: Alice pays Bob directly on-chain
cues.tradfiParallel: A gross transfer between two settlement accounts, as in an RTGS.
cues.what: Alice transfers 500,000 USDC from her reserve to Bob's on the Depository.
cues.why: Any two participants can transfer reserves on-chain: gross, and final when the block is final. The bilateral accounts that follow avoid doing this for every payment.

cues.subtitle: Hub 5,000,000 · Alice 2,500,000 · Bob 2,500,000 USDC. The total is unchanged at 10,000,000 USDC.
cues.title: Reserves in place
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: Hub 5,000,000 · Alice 2,500,000 · Bob 2,500,000 USDC. The total is unchanged at 10,000,000 USDC.
cues.why: Everything so far was on-chain. Next, two bilateral accounts take payments off-chain.

cues.subtitle: Alice and Hub open a bilateral account. Both keep an identical copy of its state, and every change is a frame both of them sign.
cues.title: Alice opens an account with Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: A correspondent relationship backed by one jointly signed record instead of two ledgers to reconcile.
cues.what: Alice and Hub open a bilateral account. Both keep an identical copy of its state, and every change is a frame both of them sign.
cues.why: The account involves only the two banks that carry its risk; nothing about it is registered network-wide.

cues.subtitle: Bob opens his own account with Hub. Alice and Bob have no account with each other; Hub connects them.
cues.title: Bob opens an account with Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: Two respondent banks using the same correspondent.
cues.what: Bob opens his own account with Hub. Alice and Bob have no account with each other; Hub connects them.
cues.why: Each bank's exposure stays inside its own account with Hub.

cues.subtitle: On a local test chain, Alice, Hub and Bob are registered on the Depository with test balances: Hub 5,000,000 · Alice 2,500,000 · Bob 2,500,000 USDC. Alice and Bob each have one bilateral account with Hub, still empty.
cues.title: Starting point: three banks, two accounts
cues.tradfiParallel: Two respondent banks with one correspondent, Hub — but each relationship is one jointly signed record, not two ledgers to reconcile.
cues.what: On a local test chain, Alice, Hub and Bob are registered on the Depository with test balances: Hub 5,000,000 · Alice 2,500,000 · Bob 2,500,000 USDC. Alice and Bob each have one bilateral account with Hub, still empty.
cues.why: Reserves sit on the Depository and belong to each bank. An account is a record both banks sign; its balance changes off-chain, frame by frame.

cues.subtitle: Alice instructs the Depository to move 500,000 USDC from her reserve into collateral for her account with Hub. The instruction goes on-chain in a batch.
cues.title: Alice posts 500,000 USDC of collateral
cues.tradfiParallel: Collateral locked per counterparty plays the nostro's role, but in a neutral contract.
cues.what: Alice instructs the Depository to move 500,000 USDC from her reserve into collateral for her account with Hub. The instruction goes on-chain in a batch.
cues.why: Collateral lets Alice pay Hub without Hub having to trust her: whatever she owes Hub in the account is covered on the Depository.

cues.subtitle: The batch waits for the next block (about 300 ms on this test chain).
cues.title: Waiting for the next block
cues.tradfiParallel: An instruction submitted to the settlement system but not yet settled.
cues.what: The batch waits for the next block (about 300 ms on this test chain).
cues.why: Until the block is final nothing has moved, so the account cannot count the collateral yet.

cues.subtitle: The block is final. Alice's reserve falls from 2,500,000 USDC to 2,000,000 USDC and her account with Hub holds 500,000 USDC of collateral. Both banks sign the account frame that records it.
cues.title: Collateral recorded on the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Pledged collateral, held by the contract rather than by Hub.
cues.what: The block is final. Alice's reserve falls from 2,500,000 USDC to 2,000,000 USDC and her account with Hub holds 500,000 USDC of collateral. Both banks sign the account frame that records it.
cues.why: Alice can now pay Hub up to 500,000 USDC off-chain, fully covered by collateral.

keyMetrics: Hub may owe Bob: up to 500,000 USDC
cues.subtitle: Bob sets a 500,000 USDC limit on what Hub may owe him in their account. Nothing is deposited; Bob and Hub both sign the new limit.
cues.title: Bob gives Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral credit limit on a correspondent, set by the bank that carries the risk.
cues.what: Bob sets a 500,000 USDC limit on what Hub may owe him in their account. Nothing is deposited; Bob and Hub both sign the new limit.
cues.why: Only the receiving bank sets this limit, and it can lower it at any time: a lower limit blocks new exposure but never erases debt already incurred. The most Hub can ever owe Bob unsecured is Bob's own limit. Intraday credit here comes from the receiving bank, not from the central bank.

cues.subtitle: Alice pays Bob 125,000 USDC through Hub. She proposes the first hop, a new frame of her account with Hub, and signs it. She sends 125,000.125 USDC: the payment plus a 0.125 USDC routing fee for Hub.
cues.title: Payment 1 of 2: Alice → Hub → Bob, 125,000 USDC
cues.tradfiParallel: A payment through one correspondent. Alice's leg is covered by her collateral; Bob's leg is a claim on Hub within the credit line Bob granted.
cues.what: Alice pays Bob 125,000 USDC through Hub. She proposes the first hop, a new frame of her account with Hub, and signs it. She sends 125,000.125 USDC: the payment plus a 0.125 USDC routing fee for Hub.
cues.why: Two accounts change, Alice–Hub and Hub–Bob, each by a frame both of its banks sign. Nothing is sent to the chain.

cues.subtitle: Hub co-signs Alice's frame and proposes the matching frame in its account with Bob.
cues.title: Hub forwards the payment to Bob
cues.tradfiParallel: A correspondent paying out against cover it has received.
cues.what: Hub co-signs Alice's frame and proposes the matching frame in its account with Bob.
cues.why: Hub passes the payment on only against the payment it already holds from Alice.

cues.subtitle: Hub now owes Bob 125,000 USDC in their account. Alice has paid Hub 125,000.125 USDC in hers, inside her collateral.
cues.title: Payment 1 complete
cues.tradfiParallel: A correspondent payment: covered on one side, a credit exposure on the other.
cues.what: Hub now owes Bob 125,000 USDC in their account. Alice has paid Hub 125,000.125 USDC in hers, inside her collateral.
cues.why: Alice's leg is covered by her collateral. Bob's leg is an unsecured claim on Hub, inside the credit line he chose.

badges.detail: Signed by both banks of each account: neither can undo it alone.
badges.label: Bilateral

badges.detail: Enforceable at the Depository up to the account's collateral: Alice's leg in full; Bob's 125,000 USDC is an unsecured claim on Hub.
badges.label: On-chain

badges.detail: Depends on whether the system is designated under settlement-finality law.
badges.label: Legal

cues.subtitle: Irrevocable between the two banks once both sign, and enforceable on-chain up to the account's collateral; above that it is an unsecured claim. Settlement in the asset happens when collateral covers it or it moves on-chain; legal finality depends on system designation.
cues.title: How final is payment 1?
cues.tradfiParallel: In an RTGS a payment settles in the settlement asset at once. Here the banks choose how much of each exposure is collateralised.
cues.what: Irrevocable between the two banks once both sign, and enforceable on-chain up to the account's collateral; above that it is an unsecured claim. Settlement in the asset happens when collateral covers it or it moves on-chain; legal finality depends on system designation.
cues.why: Bilateral finality is immediate. Settlement in the asset is bounded by collateral until the next on-chain settlement.

cues.subtitle: Same route, same rules: Alice pays Bob another 125,000 USDC through Hub.
cues.title: Payment 2 of 2: another 125,000 USDC
cues.tradfiParallel: Repeated correspondent payments with no booking in the settlement system per payment.
cues.what: Same route, same rules: Alice pays Bob another 125,000 USDC through Hub.
cues.why: A payment costs a few signatures per account, not an on-chain transaction.

cues.subtitle: Alice's collateral covers everything she has paid Hub. Hub now owes Bob 250,000 USDC with nothing posted against it.
cues.title: Payments complete: 250,000 USDC from Alice to Bob
cues.tradfiParallel: An unsecured interbank exposure inside an agreed limit.
cues.what: Alice's collateral covers everything she has paid Hub. Hub now owes Bob 250,000 USDC with nothing posted against it.
cues.why: Bob carries 250,000 USDC of unsecured exposure to Hub, within the 500,000 USDC limit he set. Rebalancing will collateralise it.

cues.subtitle: Alice's 500,000 USDC of collateral sits in the Depository, not on Hub's books: Hub can claim only the 250,000.25 USDC she has actually paid it. Bob would file the last co-signed state with the Depository. After the challenge window he is paid from Hub's remaining reserve; any shortfall is booked on-chain as Hub's debt to Bob.
cues.title: If Hub failed now
cues.tradfiParallel: Close-out against a failed correspondent. On-chain, unpaid claims queue first-come against its reserves; how that interacts with insolvency law depends on the jurisdiction.
cues.what: Alice's 500,000 USDC of collateral sits in the Depository, not on Hub's books: Hub can claim only the 250,000.25 USDC she has actually paid it. Bob would file the last co-signed state with the Depository. After the challenge window he is paid from Hub's remaining reserve; any shortfall is booked on-chain as Hub's debt to Bob.
cues.why: Debts are repaid first-come, not pro rata, from Hub's reserve on the Depository, and Hub cannot move reserves out while it owes. Bob's loss can never exceed the 500,000 USDC line he chose; today his exposure is 250,000 USDC.

cues.subtitle: Bob pays Alice 50,000 USDC through Hub, over the same two accounts in the opposite direction.
cues.title: Bob pays Alice 50,000 USDC back
cues.tradfiParallel: Bilateral netting by construction.
cues.what: Bob pays Alice 50,000 USDC through Hub, over the same two accounts in the opposite direction.
cues.why: Each account keeps one net position, so payments in opposite directions offset inside it.

cues.subtitle: Three payments, 300,000 USDC gross, leave one net position per account: Alice has paid Hub 200,000.25 USDC net, inside her collateral, and Hub owes Bob 199,999.95 USDC net. Nothing has moved on-chain.
cues.title: Net position: 200,000 USDC from Alice to Bob
cues.tradfiParallel: Continuous bilateral netting. Unlike a multilateral net settlement system, positions offset only within each pair of banks.
cues.what: Three payments, 300,000 USDC gross, leave one net position per account: Alice has paid Hub 200,000.25 USDC net, inside her collateral, and Hub owes Bob 199,999.95 USDC net. Nothing has moved on-chain.
cues.why: Gross flows stay inside the accounts; only net positions would ever need settling. The saving is bilateral only: there is no multilateral netting across accounts, and collateral is locked per counterparty instead of pooled.

cues.subtitle: Alice has paid Hub 200,000.25 USDC net, all inside her collateral. Alice and Hub co-sign a settlement: 199,999.95 USDC of the account's collateral moves to Hub's reserve.
cues.title: Rebalancing 1 of 2: settle Alice's net position against her collateral
cues.tradfiParallel: Settling the net position against pledged collateral: the obligation is discharged from the collateral, not by a new payment.
cues.what: Alice has paid Hub 200,000.25 USDC net, all inside her collateral. Alice and Hub co-sign a settlement: 199,999.95 USDC of the account's collateral moves to Hub's reserve.
cues.why: Hub is paid on-chain for what it is owed; the collateral that stays in the account is Alice's, apart from Hub's routing fees.

cues.subtitle: The Depository moved 199,999.95 USDC from the Alice–Hub collateral to Hub's reserve. The account keeps 300,000.05 USDC of collateral, of which only Hub's 0.3 USDC of routing fees is not Alice's.
cues.title: Settled on-chain: Hub's reserve +199,999.95 USDC
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: The Depository moved 199,999.95 USDC from the Alice–Hub collateral to Hub's reserve. The account keeps 300,000.05 USDC of collateral, of which only Hub's 0.3 USDC of routing fees is not Alice's.
cues.why: One on-chain transaction settles what Alice paid Hub, net, since the account opened.

cues.subtitle: Hub and Bob co-sign a settlement: Hub moves 199,999.95 USDC from its reserve into collateral for their account.
cues.title: Rebalancing 2 of 2: Hub collateralises its debt to Bob
cues.tradfiParallel: Hub collateralises its debt to Bob, as a bank posts collateral against an exposure that has grown.
cues.what: Hub and Bob co-sign a settlement: Hub moves 199,999.95 USDC from its reserve into collateral for their account.
cues.why: Hub's 199,999.95 USDC debt to Bob becomes covered on the Depository, so Bob no longer relies on credit for it.

cues.subtitle: Hub–Bob holds 199,999.95 USDC of collateral against Hub's debt to Bob, and Alice–Hub holds 300,000.05 USDC of collateral. Two on-chain settlements of 199,999.95 USDC each did it.
cues.title: Rebalanced: no uncollateralised balances right now
cues.tradfiParallel: Collateral follows exposure; the payments themselves never touched the chain.
cues.what: Hub–Bob holds 199,999.95 USDC of collateral against Hub's debt to Bob, and Alice–Hub holds 300,000.05 USDC of collateral. Two on-chain settlements of 199,999.95 USDC each did it.
cues.why: Credit lines stay open, so new payments can create unsecured exposure again until the next rebalance. The on-chain cost follows net positions and collateral policy, not the number of payments.

cues.subtitle: Alice grants Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line, so Hub can also pay her without posting collateral first.
cues.title: Alice gives Hub a credit line too
cues.tradfiParallel: A second bilateral limit, set by the bank that would carry the risk.
cues.what: Alice grants Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line, so Hub can also pay her without posting collateral first.
cues.why: With credit lines open, new payments can create unsecured exposure again.

cues.subtitle: Alice pays Hub 10,000 USDC and Hub pays Alice 5,000 USDC at the same moment. Each proposes a new frame of the same account.
cues.title: Both banks pay at the same instant
cues.tradfiParallel: Deterministic sequencing of simultaneous instructions: nothing is lost or applied twice.
cues.what: Alice pays Hub 10,000 USDC and Hub pays Alice 5,000 USDC at the same moment. Each proposes a new frame of the same account.
cues.why: A fixed rule decides which frame goes first (the bank with the lower identifier); the other is re-proposed on top of it. Both payments apply exactly once: net 5,000 USDC from Alice to Hub.

cues.subtitle: The demo now resizes the Hub–Bob account into a worst case: 100,000 USDC of collateral against a 150,000 USDC debt from Hub to Bob. Both banks sign the change.
cues.title: Stress test: what if Hub really fails?
cues.tradfiParallel: A default scenario with partial collateral.
cues.what: The demo now resizes the Hub–Bob account into a worst case: 100,000 USDC of collateral against a 150,000 USDC debt from Hub to Bob. Both banks sign the change.
cues.why: This shows what the contract does when collateral does not cover a claim.

cues.subtitle: Hub owes Bob 150,000 USDC: 100,000 USDC is covered by the account's collateral, 50,000 USDC is unsecured, inside the credit line Bob granted.
cues.title: Worst case in place
cues.tradfiParallel: A partially collateralised exposure to a correspondent.
cues.what: Hub owes Bob 150,000 USDC: 100,000 USDC is covered by the account's collateral, 50,000 USDC is unsecured, inside the credit line Bob granted.
cues.why: If Hub fails now, collateral pays first, then Hub's reserve; anything left becomes an on-chain debt.

cues.subtitle: For the test, Hub transfers its whole remaining reserve (5,099,999.95 USDC) to Alice on-chain. Nothing is left to pay unsecured claims from.
cues.title: Hub's reserve is emptied
cues.tradfiParallel: A defaulting correspondent with no liquid assets left at the settlement system.
cues.what: For the test, Hub transfers its whole remaining reserve (5,099,999.95 USDC) to Alice on-chain. Nothing is left to pay unsecured claims from.
cues.why: A failing bank may have spent or lost its reserves; this is that case.

cues.subtitle: Bob freezes his account with Hub and drafts a dispute from the last state both banks signed.
cues.title: Hub stops responding: Bob exits alone
cues.tradfiParallel: Close-out on the last confirmed position, without the defaulting party.
cues.what: Bob freezes his account with Hub and drafts a dispute from the last state both banks signed.
cues.why: Exit needs no cooperation from Hub: the last co-signed state is the evidence.

cues.subtitle: Bob submits the dispute to the Depository. Hub has 25 hours to answer with a newer co-signed state; finalizing earlier is refused. The demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.title: Bob's dispute is filed: the challenge window opens
cues.tradfiParallel: A claim with a fixed contest period.
cues.what: Bob submits the dispute to the Depository. Hub has 25 hours to answer with a newer co-signed state; finalizing earlier is refused. The demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.why: An older state loses only if the other side answers in time with a newer one, so each bank — or a watchtower — must watch the chain during the window.

cues.subtitle: The window closed with no answer. The Depository applied the last co-signed state: Bob received the 100,000 USDC of collateral. Hub's reserve was empty, so the remaining 50,000 USDC is booked on-chain as Hub's debt to Bob.
cues.title: Bob is paid from collateral; the shortfall becomes Hub's debt
cues.tradfiParallel: The Depository applies the latest co-signed state mechanically; legal finality depends on governing law. How the on-chain debt queue ranks against insolvency law is a legal question.
cues.what: The window closed with no answer. The Depository applied the last co-signed state: Bob received the 100,000 USDC of collateral. Hub's reserve was empty, so the remaining 50,000 USDC is booked on-chain as Hub's debt to Bob.
cues.why: Debts are repaid first-come, not pro rata, from Hub's reserve on the Depository, and Hub cannot move any reserve out while it owes. Bob's loss can never exceed the credit line he granted.

cues.subtitle: Alice also freezes her account with Hub and files her last co-signed state with the Depository.
cues.title: Alice exits too
cues.tradfiParallel: Recovering pledged collateral from a failed counterparty without its cooperation.
cues.what: Alice also freezes her account with Hub and files her last co-signed state with the Depository.
cues.why: Alice's collateral sits in the Depository, not on Hub's books, so she can recover her share without Hub.

cues.subtitle: Alice submits the dispute to the Depository. Hub has 25 hours to answer with a newer co-signed state; finalizing earlier is refused. The demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.title: Alice's dispute is filed: the challenge window opens
cues.tradfiParallel: A claim with a fixed contest period.
cues.what: Alice submits the dispute to the Depository. Hub has 25 hours to answer with a newer co-signed state; finalizing earlier is refused. The demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.why: An older state loses only if the other side answers in time with a newer one, so each bank — or a watchtower — must watch the chain during the window.

cues.subtitle: After the window, the Depository paid 294,999.75 USDC into Alice's reserve: her share of the account's collateral under the last co-signed state. Hub's own 5,000.3 USDC share went to Hub's reserve, where it is held for Hub's debt to Bob: Hub cannot move it out, and anyone can trigger the repayment.
cues.title: Alice recovers her collateral
cues.tradfiParallel: The Depository applies the latest co-signed state mechanically; legal finality depends on governing law.
cues.what: After the window, the Depository paid 294,999.75 USDC into Alice's reserve: her share of the account's collateral under the last co-signed state. Hub's own 5,000.3 USDC share went to Hub's reserve, where it is held for Hub's debt to Bob: Hub cannot move it out, and anyone can trigger the repayment.
cues.why: Collateral protected Alice exactly as far as it reached; the failed hub could not keep it.

cues.subtitle: A new bank, Carol, registers on the Depository with its own signing key.
cues.title: Carol joins after the failure test
cues.tradfiParallel: A new participant joining the settlement system.
cues.what: A new bank, Carol, registers on the Depository with its own signing key.
cues.why: The rest of the network keeps working: a new participant needs only its own account with a counterparty.

cues.subtitle: Carol posted 50,000 USDC of collateral, Hub granted her 25,000 USDC of credit, and Hub paid her 15,000 USDC inside their account.
cues.title: Carol has an open position with Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: Terminating a bilateral agreement with an open position: the balance is settled before the account closes.
cues.what: Carol posted 50,000 USDC of collateral, Hub granted her 25,000 USDC of credit, and Hub paid her 15,000 USDC inside their account.
cues.why: Closing an account cooperatively must settle a real position, not only an empty account.
